claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child. 

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?** 

Please let me know:
- Are they **under 16 years old**, **between 16-19 years old**, or **20 or over**?

If you have multiple children of different ages, please tell me about each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is between 16-19 years old, I need to check whether he's in full-time education or approved training. This is important because Child Benefit eligibility for 16-19 year olds depends on their education or training status.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For example, this could include:
- Full-time at school or college
- Full-time university or higher education
- An approved apprenticeship or training scheme

Please let me know his current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in full-time education. He's currently studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in full-time education studying for A-levels. Let me navigate to the next step to check the education level requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check if Alex's education meets the approved education requirements. Based on what you've told me:

**Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form college, which is approved (non-advanced) education** ✓

A-levels are on the list of approved qualifications. However, I need to confirm a couple more details:

1. **Is Alex studying at least 12 hours per week with supervised study?** (Full-time A-level study typically meets this, but please confirm)

2. **Is Alex working any paid employment?** If so, how many hours per week?

These details will help me complete the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, he's doing full-time A-levels, so definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study. 

He does have a part-time job though - he works at the local supermarket.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good to know! Alex is doing full-time A-levels with plenty of supervised study time, which meets the education requirements. However, the part-time job is an important detail I need to check.

**How many hours per week does Alex work at the supermarket?**

This is important because there are limits on how much a 16-19 year old in education can work while still qualifying for Child Benefit. Let me know the approximate hours per week, and whether it's consistent or varies.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He works full-time hours at the supermarket - it's quite a lot actually, he manages to fit it around his college schedule somehow.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. This is an important detail. When you say he works "full-time hours," can you give me a more specific number? 

**Approximately how many hours per week does Alex work at the supermarket?**

For example, is it:
- Around 30-35 hours per week?
- 40+ hours per week?
- Or something else?

This matters because if Alex is working full-time (typically defined as 16 hours or more per week, or in some cases 24+ hours depending on the specific circumstances), it could affect his eligibility for Child Benefit. I need the specific hours to check against the eligibility rules.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's around 24 hours per week - he does evenings and weekends mostly to fit it around his college timetable.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. So Alex works approximately 24 hours per week at the supermarket while studying full-time A-levels.

Let me navigate to check the rules about working hours for 16-19 year olds in education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've reached a critical point in the eligibility check. The system is asking: **Is the child working less than 24 hours per week?**

Since Alex is working approximately 24 hours per week, this is right at the threshold. However, I need to clarify:

**Is it exactly 24 hours, or is it slightly under 24 hours per week?**

This distinction is important because:
- **Less than 24 hours per week** = may be eligible (we continue checking)
- **24 hours or more per week** = not eligible

Can you confirm whether it's just under 24 hours, at 24 hours, or over 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's 24 hours or more - he does full shifts on the weekend and then some evening shifts during the week, so it adds up to at least 24 hours.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming. Unfortunately, this means Alex does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Let me navigate to the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
---

## **Eligibility Assessment Result**

**Unfortunately, you are NOT eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### **Reason:**

Alex is aged 16-19 and is working 24 or more hours per week. While he is in approved full-time education (A-levels), the combination of:
- Working 24+ hours per week, **and**
- Being in education

means he does not meet the Child Benefit eligibility requirements.

### **Key Rule:**

Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds requires them to be in approved education or training. However, children working 24+ hours per week are considered to be engaged in full-time work, which takes them outside the eligible criteria.

### **Next Steps & Alternatives:**

If Alex's work hours reduce to **less than 24 hours per week**, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to:
1. Notify HMRC of the change in circumstances
2. Provide evidence of the reduced hours
3. Your claim could then be reconsidered

For more information or to report a change in circumstances, you can:
- Visit: www.gov.uk/child-benefit
- Contact HMRC Child Benefit team

I'm sorry this wasn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about the eligibility rules?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but thank you for explaining it clearly. I understand now - it's because he's working 24 hours or more per week, even though he's still in full-time education. I appreciate you taking the time to go through everything with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could explain it clearly for you. Yes, you've understood it correctly – it's the combination of the 24+ hours of work per week that makes him ineligible, even though he's doing full-time A-levels.

Before I finish, let me formally record the outcome of this assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
If Alex's work situation changes in the future – for instance, if he reduces his hours to less than 24 per week – please don't hesitate to get back in touch or contact HMRC directly. You may be able to reclaim at that point.

Best of luck to Alex with his A-levels and his job! If you have any other questions, I'm here to help.
